name: Carne Asada — The Only Way
tagline: Skirt steak, charred lime, no shortcuts. The marinade is the recipe.
description:
Ingredients

  • 2 lb skirt steak, trimmed
  • 4 garlic cloves, smashed
  • 1 bunch cilantro, stems & all
  • 3 limes, juiced
  • 1 orange, juiced
  • 2 tbsp soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp ground cumin
  • 1 jalapeño, sliced

Method

  1. Marinade. Blitz everything except the steak. Pour over the meat. Bag it. Six hours minimum, twelve is better.
  2. Heat. The grill must scream. Smoke point or you've already failed.
  3. Sear. Two minutes per side. No moving the meat around like an amateur.
  4. Rest. Ten minutes. Under foil. Walk away.
  5. Slice. Against the grain. Thin. Salt on the cutting board.

name: Fish Tacos, San Diego
tagline: Beer battered, cabbage, crema, that's the whole law. Don't get clever.
description:
Ingredients

  • 1 lb cod or rockfish, cut into fingers
  • 1 cup flour
  • 1 cup cold lager
  • 1 tsp baking powder
  • Cabbage, shredded fine
  • Crema, lime, hot sauce
  • Corn tortillas, warmed on flame

Method

  1. Whisk the batter cold. Cold. Lumps are fine.
  2. Oil at 375°F. Test with a wooden spoon — should hiss.
  3. Dip fish, fry 3 minutes, drain on rack — never paper towels, you'll steam them soggy.
  4. Build: tortilla, fish, cabbage, crema, lime. Done.

name: Charred Little Gems
tagline: Five-minute side that costs nothing and tastes like the coast.
description:
Ingredients

  • 4 heads little gem lettuce, halved
  • 3 anchovy fillets
  • 1 egg yolk
  • 1 lemon
  • Olive oil, parmesan, black pepper

Method

  1. Cast iron, smoking hot, no oil. Lettuce cut-side down. Sixty seconds.
  2. Mash anchovies with yolk, lemon, oil. That's the dressing.
  3. Spoon over the charred lettuce. Shower of parmesan. Crack of pepper.

name: French Toast
tagline: Butter bread, egg custard, maple syrup. The bread is the whole argument.
description:
Ingredients

  • 2 large eggs
  • 4 slices Martin's Old-Fashioned Real Butter Bread
  • 1/4 cup milk
  • 1 tsp vanilla extract
  • 1/2 tsp ground cinnamon
  • Pinch of salt
  • 2 tbsp butter
  • 1/2 cup maple syrup, warmed
  • Powdered sugar, for serving

Method

  1. Crack eggs into a shallow dish. Add milk and whisk to combine.
  2. Whisk in vanilla, cinnamon, and a pinch of salt.
  3. Melt butter in a medium skillet over medium heat.
  4. Dip bread slices in egg mixture on both sides — coated, not soaked through.
  5. Fry until golden brown, about 2–3 minutes per side.
  6. Serve warm with butter and maple syrup. Powdered sugar if you want.

name: Mashed Potatoes
tagline: Russets and Yukons, a stick and a half of butter, sour cream. That's the whole secret.
description:
Ingredients

  • 3 lb. mixed potatoes (russets and Yukon Golds), peeled, cut into 1" pieces
  • Kosher salt
  • 1/2 cup whole milk
  • 3/4 cup (1 1/2 sticks) + 2 tbsp unsalted butter
  • 1/2 cup sour cream, room temperature
  • Freshly ground black pepper
  • Chopped fresh parsley, for serving

Method

  1. Cover potatoes with water in a large pot, add a generous pinch of salt. Bring to a boil and cook until softened, 15–20 minutes.
  2. Drain and return potatoes to the pot. Mash with a potato masher or ricer until smooth.
  3. While potatoes cook, warm milk and 3/4 cup butter in a small saucepan over medium-low heat until butter melts, about 3 minutes.
  4. Pour milk mixture over potatoes and stir until creamy. Add sour cream and stir to combine. Season generously with salt and pepper.
  5. Transfer to a serving bowl. Top with remaining 2 tbsp butter, more pepper, and parsley.

name: Cacio e Pepe — Properly
tagline: Three ingredients. Four if you count the water. There is nowhere to hide.
description:
Ingredients

  • 200g tonnarelli or spaghetti
  • 100g pecorino romano, finely grated
  • Black peppercorns, freshly cracked
  • Pasta water — heavily starchy

Method

  1. Toast the pepper. Dry pan, low heat, smell it bloom.
  2. Pasta in salted water — less salt than you think. The cheese is salty.
  3. Reserve a cup of water. Drain pasta one minute under.
  4. Off the heat: pecorino, splash of water, whisk to a paste. Add pasta. Toss like you mean it.
  5. If it breaks, you added cheese too hot. Start again.

name: Mexican Hot Chocolate Cookies
tagline: Cayenne, cinnamon, molten marshmallow. Chocolate cookie with a secret inside.
description:
Ingredients

  • 1½ cups / 192g all-purpose flour
  • ½ cup / 51g cocoa powder, preferably Dutch-processed
  • 1 tsp baking soda
  • 1 tsp kosher salt (Diamond Crystal)
  • ½ tsp ground cayenne
  • 3 tsp ground cinnamon (2 tsp for dough, 1 tsp for coating)
  • ½ cup / 113g unsalted butter, room temperature
  • 1½ cups / 305g light brown sugar
  • 1 large egg, room temperature
  • 2 tsp vanilla extract
  • Mini marshmallows, frozen solid
  • ¼ cup / 50g granulated sugar

Method

  1. Whisk together flour, cocoa powder, baking soda, salt, cayenne, and 2 tsp cinnamon in a medium bowl. Set aside.
  2. Beat butter and brown sugar on medium-high until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes. Add egg and vanilla. Beat until creamy, 2 more minutes. Add flour mixture and beat on low until no dry spots remain, about 1 minute.
  3. Scoop dough into 2-tablespoon mounds on a baking sheet. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, up to overnight. Freeze marshmallows if you haven't already.
  4. Heat oven to 350°F. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment. Mix the granulated sugar and remaining 1 tsp cinnamon in a small bowl.
  5. Let dough sit 5 minutes at room temperature if very stiff. Flatten a mound in your palm, pile 5 frozen marshmallows in the center, and bring the dough up and over to fully enclose them. Roll into a ball, then roll in cinnamon sugar. Place 3 inches apart on prepared sheets.
  6. Bake 10–12 minutes, rotating halfway, until cookies puff and bits of molten marshmallow peek through. Cool on the sheet 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.

Tip: Uncoated dough balls freeze for up to 3 months. To bake from frozen, thaw 5 minutes, roll in cinnamon sugar, and bake 13–15 minutes.

name: Arroz
tagline: Toasted rice, roasted garlic, tomato. The chicken broth is doing all the work.
description:
Ingredients

  • 1 cup white rice
  • 3 tomatoes, chopped
  • 5 cloves garlic
  • 1/2 onion
  • 2 cups chicken broth
  • Oil

Method

  1. Warm the chicken broth in a separate pot. Keep it hot — you'll need it.
  2. Heat a pan with oil over low heat. When warm, pour in the rice and toast, stirring occasionally.
  3. Add the garlic cloves and onion half unchopped to the rice. Stir and roast together until the rice turns light brown.
  4. Add the chopped tomatoes and enough chicken broth to just cover the rice.
  5. Cover and cook on low heat for 20 minutes.
  6. Keep a pot of hot water nearby in case the rice dries out before it's done. Do not use cold water — it will shock the rice.

name: Pozole Verde de Pollo
tagline: Tomatillo-blended broth, fall-apart chicken, three cans of hominy. The green is the whole point.
description:
Ingredients

  • 2 lb chicken thighs, bone-in
  • 1 lb tomatillos, husked and rinsed
  • 2 large white onions, divided — one for broth, one for garnish
  • 3 jalapeño peppers, halved, seeds and membranes removed
  • 2 cloves garlic
  • 1 tbsp Mexican oregano
  • 1 tsp kosher salt
  • 6 cups chicken broth
  • 1 cup cilantro, stems and leaves
  • 50 oz white hominy, drained and rinsed (3 cans)
  • 4–5 limes, halved
  • 1 bunch radishes, thinly sliced
  • ½ head cabbage, thinly shredded

Garnishes

  • Sliced radishes
  • Shredded cabbage
  • Chopped cilantro
  • Diced white onion
  • Lime wedges
  • Mexican oregano

Method

  1. Add chicken thighs, tomatillos, one rough-chopped onion, jalapeños, garlic, oregano, salt, and broth to a large pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Bring to a boil over high heat. Reduce to low, partially cover, and simmer 40 minutes until the chicken is fall-apart tender.
  3. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Shred with two forks. Set aside.
  4. Using a slotted spoon, transfer the cooked tomatillos, onion, jalapeños, and garlic to a blender. Add 1 cup of the cooking liquid and the cilantro. Blend until completely smooth.
  5. Pour the green sauce back into the pot. Stir in the shredded chicken and drained hominy.
  6. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Cook uncovered 15 minutes. Taste and season with salt and a squeeze of lime.
  7. Ladle into bowls. Serve with cabbage, radishes, cilantro, diced onion, lime wedges, and a sprinkle of oregano.

Recipe via Isabel Eats
